subject: ss-neurology
title: Neurometabolic and storage disorders: high-yield overview for NEET-PG

steps.tx: Neurometabolic and **lysosomal storage disorders** arise from enzyme or transporter defects that cause toxic substrate build-up in neurons. Many present in infancy with regression, hypotonia or seizures. Recognising a few signature signs, such as the **cherry-red spot** and **Kayser-Fleischer ring**, is often enough to name the disease in an exam.

steps.tx: Tay-Sachs disease is caused by deficiency of **beta-hexosaminidase A**, leading to GM2 ganglioside accumulation. Infants show developmental regression and an exaggerated startle to sound. The **cherry-red spot** reflects ganglion cell swelling at the macula, with the pale fovea contrasting against the normal choroid. Hepatosplenomegaly is typically absent, which helps separate it from Niemann-Pick.

steps.tx: Niemann-Pick type C is a cholesterol trafficking disorder, with **vertical gaze palsy** as a key feature. Wilson disease, caused by **ATP7B** mutations, causes copper accumulation. Its **Kayser-Fleischer ring** at the corneal Descemet membrane is a slit-lamp clue. Both can present with young-onset extrapyramidal signs, so they must be separated.

steps.tx: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation includes **PKAN** and related disorders, which show the **eye of the tiger** sign on MRI. Kufor-Rakeb syndrome, due to **ATP13A2** variants, causes juvenile parkinsonism with supranuclear gaze palsy. Dyskinesias from levodopa may be treated with amantadine in these patients.

steps.tx: Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis, the **Batten disease** group, causes progressive myoclonic epilepsy, visual failure and regression. Lipofuscin accumulates in lysosomes. Gaucher disease results from **glucocerebrosidase** deficiency and is the commonest sphingolipidosis, with splenomegaly and bone involvement, and neuronopathic forms affecting the brain.
